title: Logging inputs and outputs without leaking personal data

videos.script: To debug a bad answer you need the question. To keep the question you keep whatever the customer typed. {{tension}} In one week, every message about an order carried an order number, and an e-mail address or a phone number besides. The questions about policy carried nothing. {{scan}} So the text is cleaned before it is written. The assistant passes it through a redaction function, and the address becomes a word in brackets. {{source}} A second net sits at the exporter, for spans the assistant did not write, like the ones a library writes with the whole prompt. {{net}} Patterns miss things. A name has no shape. A model finds the names, and then calls an order number a date. {{misses}} The user becomes a keyed hash. Without the key, a list of guesses gets nowhere. {{pseudonym}} And the text gets a shorter life than the numbers. A job takes the words out after a day or a week, and leaves the counts. {{expiry}} Redaction lowers what is kept. It never makes the text anonymous. {{end}}
